newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Khaleda threatens opposition protests.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Khaleda threatens opposition protests.

text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia said on Wednesday she would launch a movement to topple the government unless it stopped what she called "terrorism" against political foes.

She was speaking at a public rally of her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) after unidentified activists attacked buses carrying her supporters to the gathering in this town southeast of Dhaka. Police said at least 20 people were injured.
"Terrorism will not be tolerated. Nor will it stop us from launching a relentless movement to protect ourselves and ensure people's rights," Khaleda told the rally.

Khaleda, whose BNP lost to Awami League in general elections last June, later announced her party would stage protest rallies countrywide on March 3 to "highlight and oppose excesses and failures by the ruling party".
In the rally witnesses quoted her as attacking Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's efforts to foster closer ties with neighbouring India.
"Let there be no doubts that we will resist anything that this government wants to accomplish in collusion with its big brothers," the former prime minister said of the moves.
Police officers said they had been unable to identify the attackers. BNP leaders alleged they were from Hasina's Awami League.
Hasina has urged her opponents not to damage the political stability she had restored after the polls.
The BNP chief also criticised Hasina for pledging to help New Delhi to fight separatist insurgents in northeast India.
"We will stand by all freedom fighters. We can't oppose them although we may not support them directly," she said.

Bangladeshi officials earlier said a recent agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi to jointly fight insurgency along their borders would also help Bangladesh battle tribal rebels in southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Some 50,000 Hill Tracts residents have fled to northeast India's Tripura state over the past few years to escape the insurgency, which officials say has killed over 8,500 people since 1973.
Khaleda said the BNP would strongly oppose any move to pull out troops from the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts.
